newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wall St, dollar brighten future for Bel-20.
newsitem.headline: Wall St, dollar brighten future for Bel-20.

text.p: The Brussels bourse took off on a bullish note in Monday trading, edged on by Wall Street's seemingly unending bull runs and a strenghthened dollar, but failed to keep its intraday high at the close.
"The Bel-20 has upward potential, with positive evolution of the dollar, Wall Street opening positive and if that continues tomorrow will look bright for for the index," said a trader.

He added that on the fundamental basis -- using traditional evaluation parameters, risk premium and yield rations -- the Bel-20 still has some perspective but the best opportunities would be for cyclical shares.
The Bel-20 closed up 6.70 points or 0.36 percent at 1,871.91, just short of the intraday high at 1,877.35.
One dealer said that with expectations of cash coming into the market just before the end of the year, people were picking up stocks to get ahead of future investors.
"We could push beyond the psychological 1,900 mark before the end of the year because interest rates look set to stay low and people have a lot of cash to invest," a dealer said.
Dealers said recent pressure from profit-taking was easing off and long-term investors were now stepping in to buy up cyclical stocks.

Dealers said investors were buying shares in plastics and chemicals firm Solvay because it supplied materials to sectors in the economy which were now benefiting from recovery, such as the construction sector.
Solvay stock was up 0.91 percent at 19,475 francs.
Utility holding company Tractebel rose 0.9 percent to 14,700 francs.

But dealers weren't impressed with the stock. "Tractebel will be a boring stock in the coming three years, the same thing happened to CBR a few years ago with the put warrant having a stabilising effect on its price", one said.
Shares in bank Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet Holding were down 1.06 percent at 2,800 francs.
"Dexia was cheap compared to other Belgian banks but now it's correctly valued compared to French bank Credit Local de France (CLF)," an analyst said.
He added it was a similar stock to CLF but more liquid and expected its price to remain around the 2,800 francs mark.
One steel analyst said he was positive about the steel wire and cord manufacturer Bekaert which fell 0.19 percent at 26,200 francs.
